summary: Dining Club Phase 2/3/4 backend is GREEN (14/14 pytest cases pass). Merchant self-serve (enroll/me/locations/capacity/meals/analytics/webhooks add-list-delete), non-owner 400 guards, resume endpoint GET /selection/{id}, spin `segments`+`winner_index` payload, and the full redeem → Stripe-Connect payout ledger cycle (gross 999 / platform_fee 100 / net 899 / settlement pending_no_connect for demo-seeded restaurants) are all verified end-to-end. WEB UI: /dining/merchant renders correctly for test@ (Restaurant Portal, Stripe Connect onboarding_in_progress, Performance stats, Locations w/ capacity, Today's Veg/Non-Veg meal editors, Add location, POS WEBHOOKS list w/ delete). MOBILE (Expo web preview): Home shows RadioLife Dining Club CTA, /dining renders enrollment card, /dining/play renders warm-cream themed picker (Veg/Non-Veg + Lunch/Dinner + Find my restaurants). CRITICAL FINDING: virtually ALL spec-required test IDs are ABSENT on BOTH web AND mobile (dining-home, dining-play, dining-merchant-page, dining-use-meal-btn, dining-pref-veg, dining-pref-nonveg, dining-period-lunch, dining-period-dinner, dining-spin-btn, dining-surprise-btn, dining-accept-btn, dining-reroll-btn all count=0). MOBILE preview integration additionally breaks due to CORS (expo.preview.emergentagent.com blocked hitting preview.emergentagent.com/api/* — backend responds with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` which browsers reject when the frontend sends credentials/cookies). As a result, mobile /dining shows the enrollment form even for demo@ (who is already subscribed) because the /api/dining-club fetch was rejected. Phase 1 regression (via iter126) remains fully green. No red-screen or blocking crashes on either surface — pages render, they just lack testids and mobile-preview API integration.

minor.issue: Currently only requires current_user (cookie) — no merchant-role guard; any authed user with a QR token can redeem. In iter127 the redeem was executed successfully as `admin@` on demo@'s order to verify ledger. Add a guard: (a) require the caller be a dining merchant owner, (b) require location_id belongs to that merchant, and (c) verify location.merchant_id matches the qr_token's redemption target. Reference: /app/backend/routes/dining_club.py:402

Stripe Connect onboarding failure is logged as warning and swallowed — enroll always returns 200 with `connect_onboarding_url:null`. Consider surfacing a structured status ('stripe_error'/'network_error') so the merchant dashboard can show a retry CTA instead of silently rendering an incomplete state. Reference: /app/backend/routes/dining_club.py:485

Backend advertises `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` but the browser rejects * when the frontend sends `credentials: 'include'` (cookies) or `Authorization` with `withCredentials`. This blocks the Expo web preview (origin `https://mobile-games-v2.expo.preview.emergentagent.com`) from calling `preview.emergentagent.com/api/*`. Native mobile builds work; QA-via-web-preview cannot exercise the API flows. Recommend echoing the request `Origin` when it matches an allowlist, plus `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Reference: backend CORS middleware configuration (CORS_ORIGINS='*').

critical_code_review_comments: services.dining_club.spin returns `segments` as an integer count (the slice count), not an array of segment metadata. The web+mobile Wheel components already consume it as N (renders N equal slices). If the review spec expected an array of {restaurant_id,name,color} per segment (for labeled slices), the current implementation only supports blind N-slice rendering — acceptable given the 'hidden until result' contract, but note the API surface deviates from the human-readable spec wording.

routes/dining_club.merchant_redeem: no role/ownership check on the caller. Any authed cookie can redeem a leaked qr_token. This was successfully exploited as admin@ in iter127's payout-ledger test. Add: `m = await _owned(db, user)` and verify the QR's location.merchant_id == m.merchant_id.

routes/dining_club.merchant_enroll: silently swallows Stripe Connect exceptions (logger.warning + return with connect_onboarding_url=None). A first-time enrollee whose Stripe call fails gets 200 + null URL with no indication of what went wrong. Return {stripe_error:'…'} in the payload or 502 so the UI can retry.

The /api/merchant/dining-club/redeem body includes optional `location_id` (used for stronger validation) — but nothing enforces it. Consider making it required for a defense-in-depth check that the scanning location matches the QR's target.

CORS: `CORS_ORIGINS="*"` combined with credentialed fetches will always be blocked by browsers. Since the mobile Expo web preview host is stable per-slug, add it to an allowlist and set `allow_credentials=True` with an explicit origin echo.

rca of the issue: Root cause of missing testIDs: the four /pages/dining/*.jsx web pages and three /mobile/app/dining/*.tsx screens were built with human-readable UI copy but the code review comments' checklist item 'All interactive and key informational elements have a stable test id to facilitate robust automated testing' was not applied. Fix is mechanical — add data-testid (web) / testID (mobile) props to each container/CTA/toggle following the spec identifiers. Root cause of mobile CORS block: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` cannot be combined with credentialed requests (browsers block for security). Since mobile fetches send Authorization: Bearer + include cookies in some paths, the Expo web preview origin (`expo.preview.emergentagent.com`) is refused. Native EAS/Expo Go builds do not enforce browser CORS, so this is a preview-QA-only issue but it prevents pre-launch automated verification via web-preview.
